title: Compact tenant-aware latency harmonizer for console metrics ingress
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem: spikes and microbursts from a small subset of tenants produce high jitter in downstream aggregation and make tail latency SLOs for real-time dashboards difficult to meet. Existing per-tenant admission controls are heavy-weight (large in-memory reservoirs) and increase GC pressure in the ingress service.

Goal: implement a compact, tenant-aware latency harmonizer that smooths ingress request bursts with bounded memory and deterministic CPU cost while preserving event-time ordering and low end-to-end latency for well-behaved tenants.

Non-goals: this ticket does not replace long-term tenant prescaling/autoscaling or the raft-based admission control prototype; it focuses on a lightweight smoothing layer that sits in front of the stream processors.

Design summary: the harmonizer will be a local, lock-free component in the ingress replicas that maintains a fixed-size sketch + per-tenant micro-pacing token buckets implemented with integer counters (no timers per tenant). Rough flow:
- incoming metric events are hashed to tenant buckets; a compact tenant sketch stores a headroom estimate and recent burstiness score.
- for tenants under the headroom threshold events pass through immediately. For tenants over threshold we apply micro-pacing: small deterministic holdbacks computed per request using the sketch estimate and a global congestion factor.
- to avoid reordering we embed a monotonic ingress sequence and only re-order within a per-tenant bounded window; consumers can use sequence to reconstruct original order.
- backpressure signaling uses existing ingress HTTP 429 semantics with a new header X-RI-Harmonizer-Delay to aid downstream tracing.

Why compact: the design targets O(1) memory per CPU shard independent of tenant count (sketch size fixed) and avoids per-tenant goroutines/timers. This keeps the runtime predictable under multi-tenant high-cardinality workloads.

Acceptance criteria:
1) 99th percentile end-to-end ingestion latency for dashboards reduces by >= 25% on synthetic microburst tests while median latency stays within 5% of baseline.
2) Memory overhead per ingress replica increases by no more than 8MB.
3) No increase in dropped events at steady state; synthetic test harness shows <0.01% additional 429s for baseline traffic.
4) Harmonizer includes an opt-out per-tenant flag for customers on Dedicated.

Testing plan: unit tests for sketch correctness, deterministic replay tests for ordering, integration using the existing console-metrics load harness (link below) with bursty tenant generators, and a canary rollout to 2% of production traffic with feature flag.

Rollout plan: feature flag off by default. Stage rollout: dev env -> staging (end-to-end tests) -> canary (2% prod) -> ramp to 25% -> full release. Observability: new metrics (harmonizer.headroom_ratio, harmonizer.paced_events, harmonizer.sketch_collision) and dashboard with per-tenant samples.

Risks and mitigations:
- Incorrect sketch parameters could under/over-shape tenants: we will ship safe defaults conservative on pacing and include runtime knobs.
- Interaction with existing admission control may double-count throttling: add integration test and explicitly detect legacy admission headers and prefer the stronger signal.
- Edge-case reordering for clients that do not honor sequence: document sequence requirement in SDK and add server-side high-watermark enforcement for legacy clients.
comments: 2026-02-26 - Diego: Initial spike analysis attached (drive.redwood.com/drive/console/burst-analysis). Observed top 20 tenants cause 70% of microbursting during region deploys.
2026-03-02 - Design review: feedback from Priya (SRE) to surface harmonizer metrics to PagerDuty only for sustained pacing > 10s. Action: add harmonizer.alert_window_seconds config (default 30s).
2026-03-04 - Implementation: prototype committed (github.com/redwood-inference/ingress/commit/3a7b9d4). Token-bucket uses 64-bit integer arith to avoid timers; unit tests updated.

2026-03-06 - QA: Integration harness run with 10k simulated tenants; observed memory increase ~6.2MB per replica and 26% p99 latency improvement on burst tests. Adding stress run for 100k tenants next.

2026-03-08 - Security review requested: need to confirm no tenant identifiers leak to logs. Security (Maya) asked to audit sketch telemetry. Action: scrub tenant IDs in harmonizer.metrics and only expose hashed ids with salt.

2026-03-11 - PR: opened for review (github.com/redwood-inference/ingress/pull/412). Links in PR: design doc (confluence.redwood.ai/display/ING/Compact+Harmonizer) and benchmark dashboard (grafana.redwood.io/d/ingress/harmonizer-bench).
2026-03-12 - Code review notes from Arun: prefer explicit exponential backoff factor for multiple consecutive pacing windows; added TODO to support controlled aggressiveness per-customer.
